subject: Re: Aperture Health pilot — initial scope, success metrics & owners
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Matthew Sanders <matthew.sanders@aperturehealth.com>
Cc: Priya Rao <priya@aperturehealth.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 3 Sep 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Aperture Health pilot — initial scope, success metrics & owners

Hi Matthew / Priya — great conversation today, thanks for walking through the primary use cases. Per our call, I wanted to capture a concise post-call recap and proposed next steps so we have a single source of truth to share with your team and ours.

Summary of the ask
- Aperture: deploy a short pilot that validates Redwood inference for extractive summarization of clinical intake forms and a downstream triage classifier for routing.
- Success horizon: 4 weeks of active testing after baseline integration.

What we propose for the Pilot (POC)
1) Scope: run both models against a 10k-message sample (we can start with the 1k sample you shared). Deliverables: weekly KPI digest, per-route latency/throughput report, sample outputs for QA.
2) Evaluation plan: run parallel evaluations vs. your current rule-based pipeline on precision/recall for triage and ROUGE-L for summaries. Also capture subjective QA scoring from your clinical reviewers.
3) Success criteria (initial draft):
   - Latency: p95 generation latency < 350ms for summary route (90th percentile for triage classification < 150ms).
   - Throughput: sustain 40 reqs/sec across the pilot pool with <2% error rate.
   - Cost: average cost/token <= $0.0008 (target; we will report both model and infra components).
   - Quality: triage macro-F1 >= 0.88 vs. labeled holdout; summaries average ROUGE-L improvement >= 15% vs. current baseline; clinical QA pass rate >= 85% for high-priority cases.
4) Owners / engagements
   - Redwood: integration support (Neha) and performance tuning (Rishi).
   - Aperture: dataset access, labeled holdout, weekly QA feedback loop (Matthew / Priya).

Next steps (proposed timeline)
- Week 0 (this week): sign mutual action plan + get sample data (1k).
- Week 1: integration + smoke tests.
- Week 2–3: calibration runs and metric collection.
- Week 4: readout and decision (pass / iterate / stop).

I attached a short POC scope doc and a lightweight KPI template. Can you confirm that the targets above look reasonable and whether Aperture can commit to providing the labeled holdout by Mon, Sep 6?

Thanks — I’ll wait for confirmation and will surface an internal owner map for tracking.

Best,
Dylan
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

[attachments: aperture_poc_scope.pdf, redwood_kpi_template.xlsx]

From: Matthew Sanders <matthew.sanders@aperturehealth.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Rao <priya@aperturehealth.com>
Date: Mon, 6 Sep 2027 09:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Aperture Health pilot — initial scope, success metrics & owners

Thanks Dylan — appreciate the speedy recap. The targets look mostly reasonable; a few clarifications: 

1) Latency: the 350ms target for summaries is aggressive — our current infra averages ~500ms p95 for similar-length inputs. If Redwood can get us to <350ms that would be a clear win; happy to mark that as a stretch target if needed.
2) Throughput: 40 reqs/sec is fine for the pilot traffic profile.
3) Cost: Aperture has an internal threshold of $0.0010/token for any production decision; if the pilot reports lower that's great.
4) Quality: we can commit to providing a 2k labeled holdout by Sep 8 (our ML team will prioritize). Clinical reviewers can run QA checks twice during the pilot, week 2 and week 4.

Two asks from our side:
- Please include a lightweight stability gate: <1% server-side errors and <0.5% malformed output cases.
- Is Redwood able to provide KV/prefix caching suggestions for repeated patient follow-ups? That will be important for reducing cost on repeated contexts.

If we can get an adjusted doc with the stability gate and caching notes, I'll loop in procurement for the pilot MSA.

—Matthew
Director of Product
Aperture Health

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Matthew Sanders <matthew.sanders@aperturehealth.com>
Cc: Priya Rao <priya@aperturehealth.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 7 Sep 2027 11:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Aperture Health pilot — initial scope, success metrics & owners

Thanks Matthew — great, appreciated. Quick updates inline and a couple of clarifications from the Redwood ops side.

- Latency: we can accept the summary latency as a stretch target. For pilot readouts we'll report both baseline (no optimizations) and optimized (batching + quantization/compilation) numbers. Goal: optimized p95 < 350ms.
- Stability gate: added — server-side errors <1% and malformed outputs <0.5%.
- Caching: yes — Redwood supports prefix/KV caching. We'll provide a short caching config that should reduce token re-generation for repeated patient contexts (we'll include config suggestions in the shared Drive).

Attached is an updated KPI sheet that includes the stability gate and two columns for baseline vs optimized performance. We also attached a small sample test set (anonymized) to validate integration semantics.

Internal owners (for clarity):
- Integration & onboarding: Neha Kapoor — primary SRE/SE contact for API keys, VPC details, test harness.
- Performance tuning & quantization experiments: Rishi Malhotra — will run small-scale profiling jobs and recommend model/quantization pairings.
- Customer success/readout: Dylan Brooks — coordinate weekly check-ins and the final readout deck.

Next steps (confirmed):
1) Aperture to confirm labeled holdout delivery by EOD Sep 8 (Matt).
2) Redwood to provision pilot pool and share caching config + KPI sheet by EOD Sep 7.
3) Kickoff integration call on Sep 9 (propose 10:00 AM PT) — please confirm availability.

If that timeline works, I'll route the mutual action plan and copy procurement links.

Best,
Dylan

[attachments: redwood_kpi_template.xlsx, sample_test_set.csv]

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 8 Sep 2027 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Aperture POC — internal readiness checklist

Dylan / Rishi — quick internal checklist ahead of the Sep 9 kickoff: 
- I have created a dedicated pilot pool (2 gpus, autoscale burst to 4) in us-west-2.
- API keys: sandbox keys generated and uploaded to the shared Drive folder.
- Caching config draft: added to Drive (prefix_cache: enabled; ttl=3600s; keying: patient_id + encounter_id).
- Test harness: sample ingestion script ready (ingest_sample.py) and can consume CSV rows from sample_test_set.csv.

Notes / risks:
- We should log early if we hit >300ms p95 on summaries in baseline — call out to product for a quick compilation pass.
- Need to ensure we redact PHI in the sample test set; I anonymized local copies but confirm Aperture's final dataset is compliant.

I'll be on the kickoff and can drive verification runs. Rishi — can you schedule a 2-hour profiling window in Week 2 for quantization experiments?

-Neha

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Cc: Matthew Sanders <matthew.sanders@aperturehealth.com>, Priya Rao <priya@aperturehealth.com>
Date: Thu, 9 Sep 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Aperture Health pilot — kickoff confirmed (Sep 9 10:00 AM PT)

All — confirming kickoff at Sep 9 10:00 AM PT (calendar invite sent). Quick technical commitments from my side: 
- I'll run an initial profiling pass during the integration day to capture token-level cost and baseline latency (no quant).
- If baseline p95 > 300ms, I will attempt a compilation + int8 quantization pass and re-run the benchmark same day.
- Deliverable week 1: baseline report + optimization plan. Week 2 deliverable: quantized throughput numbers and a short tuning playbook.

Matthew / Priya: please accept the invite and ensure the labeled holdout link is shareable by Sep 9 9:30 AM. If procurement needs the MSA to be attached, circle back to Dylan; we have a standard pilot MSA template.

Thanks — excited to get going.
Rishi
